chapter_title: Automated Checks, Cost, and Student Privacy
learning_objective: The learner will apply risk-matched oversight to choose send back, check every claim, or spot-check for each of eight features of agent reports, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** human-check-planner
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** apply
**Learning Objective:** The learner will apply risk-matched oversight to choose send back, check every claim, or spot-check for each of eight features of agent reports, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Human in the Loop, and the sections on agent scoring and agent evaluation reports in Chapter 12 (all defined in this chapter above this block or in Chapter 12). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each feature the learner commits one of three responses. A response is correct when it matches the Correct response column in Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Reading the oversight levels is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A report with numbers is trustworthy. (2) A person must redo every score. (3) A rule-breaking report can be fixed by hand. **Instructional Rationale:** Choosing a response from a risk rule is an Apply-level action. Eight report features that map to three responses teach the learner to read a report for the signs that need attention. **Content:** The three responses: Send back (the report breaks a rule of the rubric or the prompt, so the agent must run again), Check every claim (the report may follow the rules, but its claims rest on the agent's own word), and Spot-check (the report follows the rules and shows exact evidence, so a person verifies a sample). The eight features: | # | Feature of an agent report shown to the learner | Correct response | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | The total is 71, and the ten metric scores add up to 68. | Send back | The arithmetic is wrong, and the report breaks its own rule. | | 2 | The decision is Adopt for a resource with a total of 76 and one metric at 4. | Send back | The decision breaks the adoption rule, which needs every metric at 5 or more. | | 3 | An alignment score of 7 with no evidence quoted. | Send back | The prompt required evidence for every score. | | 4 | A factual accuracy score of 9 that rests on the agent's own knowledge, with no sources. | Check every claim | No source is cited, so each claim must be checked. | | 5 | A statement that all links work, with no link-checker log attached. | Check every claim | The claim may be invented, and the test must be run again. | | 6 | An open license score of 9, with footer evidence on 6 of 6 pages and a tool log. | Spot-check | The evidence is exact and checkable, so a sample is enough. | | 7 | A reading level from a tool, with the grade numbers shown. | Spot-check | The numbers are in the tool log, and a person can recompute one. | | 8 | An editable source score of 10, with a file list and all ten check results. | Spot-check | The evidence is complete and verifiable. | **Provenance:** The features are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The responses follow the chapter section "Human in the Loop". **Rules:** Each feature has exactly one correct response. Three features are Send back, two are Check every claim, and three are Spot-check. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one feature and the three responses. 2. The learner may open the oversight levels. Opening them does not change the score. 3. The learner chooses a response, and the choice is committed. 4. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 5. After feature 8 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 features in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [response]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The response is [response]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can match the check to the risk." Below 7 it lists the Why text of each missed feature. **Starting State:** The first feature and the three responses. The question shown is "How much checking does this report need?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says rule-breaking reports go back, claims with no source are checked in full, and well-evidenced reports are spot-checked.
